label: In code (Python, JavaScript, Java, C++ and similar), a list or array being started, typed or grown: strongest for an empty list literal or empty list constructor that is about to be filled, a List/ArrayList/vector type or type hint, or adding one item to the end of it (append, push); a list literal that already holds items fires more weakly, and so does technical prose saying something returns a list or array. Dicts, sets, tuples, plain numbers and 'list' in everyday prose stay quiet; a variable only named with 'list' can fire weakly.

probed_before.source: this checkout's .probe-log, before the pre-registration commit

qc.label_under_test: In code (Python, JavaScript, Java, C++ and similar), a list or array being made or typed (an empty or filled [] literal, list(), or a List, ArrayList, Array or vector type or type hint) or grown by adding an item to it (append, push), plus technical text saying something returns a list. Removing items (pop), dicts, sets, tuples and plain numbers stay quiet, and so does 'list' in everyday prose; a variable that is only named with 'list' can fire weakly.
